ownerThemes.theme: Owners who moved from a domestic machine say the oil pan means no oiling routine and the stitch is balanced and consistent; one paid about $900 for a complete set.
First-industrial buyers report they rarely touch the domestic machine afterward and wish they had bought sooner.
New owners ask about servo motor setup, speed control and bobbin winding while sewing; the long production run means parts and advice are easy to find.
DIY table bundles draw complaints about poor or missing assembly instructions; others found the included instructions adequate.

crossShop.why: The other Juki single-needle lockstitch sold to home shops; same 5,500 spm class, usually a little cheaper and not marketed as made in Japan.
Buyers sewing leather, vinyl or canvas find the drop-feed DDL is the wrong tool and step up to the walking foot machine.
The portable straight-stitch alternative for anyone without floor space for a 48 in industrial table.

editorial.verdict: The DDL-5550 is a made-in-Japan industrial straight stitch head that does one thing at 5,500 spm and needs a table, a motor and floor space to do it.
editorial.whoFor: A home shop sewing garments, bags or quilts in volume who wants an industrial lockstitch with a long parts history and is willing to give up zigzag entirely.
editorial.skipIf: You sew leather, vinyl or thick canvas (that is a walking foot job), or you have no room for a 48 by 20 in table.
editorial.keySpec: 5,500 spm · 5 mm stitch length · 13 mm knee lift · DBx1 needle
strengths: Automatic lubrication with an oil pan, so there is no per-session oiling routine.

weaknesses: Straight stitch only; no zigzag, no buttonhole, no free arm.
Sold as a head; the table, stand and motor come from the dealer and DIY bundles ship unassembled with thin instructions.

checks.title: 5550 or 5550N, and which suffix
checks.body: Today's stock is the DDL-5550N. NA is set up for light fabric, NH for heavy fabric with a size 21 needle, and N-7 adds an automatic thread trimmer at a higher price. Confirm which one the listing ships.

checks.title: Servo or clutch motor
checks.body: Most current bundles include a servo motor with a speed dial, which is what a home shop wants. Older or cheaper bundles may ship a clutch motor that runs at one speed and is loud at idle.

checks.title: Assembled or DIY table
checks.body: Some dealers ship the table assembled with the head mounted. Marketplace bundles ship a flat-pack table, motor and head separately and expect you to mount and belt them.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the Juki DDL-5550 and DDL-5550N?
faqs.a: They are the same machine under the current name. Juki now sells it as the DDL-5550N; variants add a letter for light (NA) or heavy (NH) material setups, and N-7 adds an automatic thread trimmer.

faqs.q: Is the DDL-5550 a walking foot machine?
faqs.a: No. It is a drop-feed single-needle lockstitch for light to medium-heavy materials. For leather, vinyl or heavy canvas Juki's walking foot model is the DNU-1541S.

faqs.q: How fast does the DDL-5550 sew?
faqs.a: Juki lists 5,500 stitches per minute for medium-weight material and 4,000 spm for light and heavy-weight setups. A servo motor lets you dial it far lower.

faqs.q: Does the DDL-5550 come with a motor?
faqs.a: Not from Juki. It is sold as a head. Dealers bundle a table, stand and a servo motor; check the listing for which motor is included.

faqs.q: How much does the DDL-5550 weigh?
faqs.a: Not published in the results captured. One dealer snippet says about 75 lb for the head alone; the table and motor add more. Treat the figure as unverified.

faqs.q: How much room is there to the right of the needle?
faqs.a: Not published in the results captured. Juki describes the arm space as wide enough for easy handling but gives no inch figure in the snippets found.

faqs.q: What needles does the DDL-5550 use?
faqs.a: DBx1 industrial needles. Juki ships it with a size 14 and lists sizes 9 to 18.

faqs.q: Does the DDL-5550 have an automatic thread trimmer?
faqs.a: Not on the base model. The DDL-5550N-7 variant adds automatic trimming and costs more.

faqs.q: Is the DDL-5550 made in Japan?
faqs.a: Juki correspondence quoted by a seller says the DDL-5550N is made in Japan, and dealer titles say so. The DDL-8700 is not marketed that way.
